result:
I fixed every rule in `pricebook.py` that didn't match its docstring. I tested all 150 rules against a reference built straight from each docstring and the module rules, across about 3,900 qty/unit pairs per rule. Before the fix 10 rules failed; after it none do.

**Rules whose results were wrong (10)**

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 05, 16, 92 | The cap was applied to the price before the discount was worked out. The module says the cap goes on the discount, not the price. | Work out the discount first, then `min(disc, cap)` |
| 11 | Used `qty > 50`, so exactly 50 units got no discount ("50+" should include 50) | `qty >= 50` |
| 19, 80, 131 | Used `round(...)`, which can round up. The module says discounts are always rounded down to the won. | `// 100` |
| 30 | Same `round()` problem on a whole rule | `base * 15 // 100` |
| 77 | Labelled marginal but discounted the full amount | `(qty - 10) * unit * 12 // 100` |
| 82 | The 100,000 won cap only kicked in once the discount passed 200,000, so discounts between 100,000 and 200,000 weren't capped | Always `min(disc, 100000)` |

**Threshold conditions fixed for clarity (results unchanged)**

- **Rule 47** had `qty >= 101` and **Rule 72** had `qty > 20`. These are marginal rules, so the discount at exactly the threshold is 0 and the answer comes out the same either way. I changed them to `>= 100` and `>= 20` so the code says what the docstring says.

All changes are in `pricebook.py`, and I didn't touch the docstrings. The test script is in my scratchpad, not the project. The project has no test file of its own.

STATUS: DONE
